chapter.heading: Zophar Urges Job to Repent
chapter.v:
Then Zophar
the Naamathite answered and said: [Job 5:7; Eccl.]

“Should not
the multitude of words be answered?And should a man full of talk be vindicated? [Job 8:9; Ps. 103:15; 144:4; Is. 40:6; James 1:10, 11; 1 Pet. 1:24]

Should your
empty talk make men hold their peace?And when you mock, should no one rebuke you? [Ps. 8:4; 144:3 d [Ps. 143:2]]

For you
have said,‘My doctrine is pure,And I am clean in your eyes.’ [[Job 15:14; 25:4; Ps. 51:2, 5, 10; John 3:6; Rom. 5:12; Eph. 2:3]]

But oh,
that God would speak,And open His lips against you, [Job 7:1; 21:21; Heb. 9:27]

That He
would show you the secrets of wisdom!For they would double your prudence.Know therefore that God exacts from youLess than your iniquity deserves. [Job 7:16, 19; Ps. 39:13 h Job 7:1]

“Canyou search
out the deep things of God?Can you find out the limits of the Almighty?

They are
higher than heaven— what can you do?Deeper than Sheol— what can you know?

Their measure
is longer than the earthAnd broader than the sea.

“IfHe passes
by, imprisons, and gathers to judgment,Then who can hinder Him? [Job 10:21,]

For He
knows deceitful men;He sees wickedness also.Will He not then consider it?

For an
empty-headed man will be wise,When a wild donkey’s colt is born a man.

“If you
would prepare your heart,And stretch out your hands toward Him;

Because you
would forget your misery,And remember it as waters that have passed away, [Job 10:6, 14; Ps. 56:8; 139:1-3; Prov. 5:21; [Jer.]

And your
life would be brighter than noonday.Though you were dark, you would be like the morning. [Deut. 32:32-]

And you
would be secure, because there is hope;Yes, you would dig around you, and take your rest in safety.

You would
also lie down, and no one would make you afraid;Yes, many would court your favor.

But the
eyes of the wicked will fail,And they shall not escape,And their hope—loss of life!”
